newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer agrees to Highlands plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer agrees to Highlands plan.

text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Tuesday that Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc had agreed to Highlands' restructuring plan and that Placer Dome would pay Highlands A$316.1 million to buy Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
As part of the restructuring plan, Highlands said that its new entity Highlands Pacific would raise at least A$160 million of new equity at an issue price of 30 cents per share.
"It is intended to provide priority to Highlands Gold shareholders in the capital raising," Highlands said.

The restructuring plan involves all shares in Highlands other than those held by Placer being cancelled and holders receiving a capital return of 65 cents cash per share and one share in Highlands Pacific.
Placer's agreement to the plan is subject to the satisfactory completion by this Friday of A$160 million of underwriting for the issue by Highlands Pacific.

"It is proposed that the shareholding entitlement in Highlands Pacific otherwise attributable to Placer will be placed, and that Highlands Pacific will also raise new capital to secure funding for the final feasibility study on Ramu, further work on Frieda-Nena and the ongoing exploration programme," Highlands said.
"We am pleased that Placer has accepted our offer", Highlands managing director Ian Goddard said.

"There has been strong institutional interest in our proposal which unlocks the value of Ramu, Frieda-Nena and Highlands' extensive exploration interests. We are looking forward to finalising the underwriting by the end of the week," Goddard said.

Placer Dome said in a separate statement that the A$316.1 million (US$249.7 million) paid for the 25 percent stake in Porgera was equivalent to the high point of a valuation prepared by Baring Bros Burrows and Co.

Last month Placer offered to buy Highlands' stake in Porgera for A$276.8 million. Placer already holds a separate 25 percent stake in Porgera through its Placer Pacific Ltd unit, the operator of the giant one million ounce-a-year mine.
Placer held 40.8 percent of Highlands before its 75 cent per share full takeover bid for Highlands announced last month.
Highlands Gold shares were unchanged at 79 cents at 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT).
